Three different clefs are used: the G-clef (G4), the C-clef (C4), and the F-clef (F3).

15740.etyen:
Compound of f (“F (the musical note)”) + nøkkel (“clef, key”), literally “F key”. The letter goes back to Latin F, from Etruscan 𐌅 (v), from Ancient Greek Ϝ (W, “digamma”), from Phoenician 𐤅 (w, “waw”). The second component continues Middle Norwegian nykill, from Old Norse lykill (“key”), from Proto-Germanic *lukilaz, derived from *lūkaną (“to close, shut”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *lewg- (“to bend, turn”). Its musical sense is modelled on Italian chiave and French clef (“key; clef”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk f-nøkkel, f-nykel, Danish F-nøgle, Icelandic f-lykill, German F-Schlüsse
